title: Prophetic birds cannot foresee their own danger
source_text: ἡμῖν δ᾿ ὀλίγα πρὸς τὰ προκείμενα ἀπὸ πολλῶν λεκτέον, διελέγχουσι τὴν ἀχάριστον ψευδοδοξίαν πρὸς τὸν πεποιηκότα αὐτόν· „ἄνθρωπος“ γὰρ καὶ Κέλσος ὢν „ἐν τιμῇ ὢν οὐ συνῆκε,“ διὸ οὐδὲ „παρασυνεβλήθη“ τοῖς ὄρνισι καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις (ἀλόγοις) ζῴοις, οἷς νομίζει εἶναι μαντικοῖς, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκείνοις παραχωρήσας τὰ πρωτεῖα ὑπὲρ Αἰγυπτίους, τοὺς τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα ὡς θεοὺς προσκυνοῦντας, ἑαυτὸν ὑπέταξε τὸ δ᾿ ὅσον ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ καὶ πᾶν τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος ὡς χεῖρον καὶ ἔλαττον νοοῦν περὶ τοῦ θείου τοῖς ἀλόγοις ζῴοις. προηγουμένως μὲν οὖν ζητείσθω, πότερον ὑπάρχει ἡ δι᾿ ὀρνίθων καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ζῴων, πεπιστευμένων εἶναι μαντικῶν, μαντικὴ ἢ μὴ ὑπάρχει. καὶ γὰρ οὐκ εὐκαταφρόνητός ἐστιν εἰς ἑκάτερα ἐπιχειρούμενος ὁ λόγος· ὅπου μὲν δυσωπῶν μὴ παραδέξασθαι τὸ τοιοῦτον, ἵνα μὴ τὸ λογικὸν ἀντὶ τῶν δαιμονίων χρηστηρίων ὄρνισι χρήσηται, καταλιπὸν ἐκεῖνα, ὅπου δὲ διὰ μαρτυρουμένης ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἐναργείας παριστὰς ὅτι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ μεγίστων διεσώθησαν κινδύνων, πεισθέντες τῇ δι᾿ ὀρνίθων μαντικῇ. ἐπὶ δὲ τοῦ παρόντος δεδόσθω ὑπαρκτὸν εἶναι τὴν οἰωνιστικὴν, ἵνα καὶ οὕτως δείξω τοῖς προκαταληφθεῖσιν ὅτι καὶ τούτου διδομένου πολλή ἐστιν ἡ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παρὰ τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα καὶ παρ᾿ αὐτὰ τὰ μαντικὰ ὑπεροχὴ καὶ οὐδαμῶς πρὸς ἐκεῖνα συγκριτή. λεκτέον ουν ὅτι, εἴπερ τις θεία φύσις ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς τῶν μελλόντων προγνωστικὴ καὶ ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον πλουσία, ὡς ἐκ περιουσίας καὶ τῷ βουλομένῳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων δηλοῦν τὰ ἐσόμενα, δηλονότι πολὺ πρότερον τὰ περὶ ἑαυτῶν ἐγίνωσκον· (γινώσκον) τα δὲ τὰ περὶ ἑαυτῶν ἐφυλάξατο (αν) ἀναπτῆναι κατὰ τοῦδε τοῦ τόπου, ἐφ᾿ οὗ παγίδας καὶ δίκτυα ἄνθρωποι ἔστησαν κατ᾿ αὐτῶν, ἢ τοξόται σκοπῷ χρώμενοι τοῖς ἱπταμένοις βέλη ἐπ᾿ αὐτὰ ἀπέλυον. πάντως δ᾿ ἂν καὶ προγινώσκοντες ἀετοὶ τὴν κατὰ τῶν νεοσσῶν ἐπιβουλὴν, εἴτε τῶν ἀναβαινόντων πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὄφεων καὶ διαφθειρόντων αὐτοὺς, εἴτε καί τινων ἀνθρώπων εἴτ᾿ εἰς παιδιὰν εἴτε καὶ εἰς ἄλλην τινὰ χρείαν καὶ θεραπείαν λαμβανόντων αὐτοὺς, οὐκ ἂν ἐνόσσευσαν ἔνθα ἔμελλον ἐπιβουλεύεσθαι· καὶ ἁπαξαπλῶς οὐκ ἄν ποτε τῶν ζῴων τι τούτων ἁλωτὸν ἀνθρώποις ἦν ὡς ἀνθρώπων θειότερον καὶ σοφώτερον.
pass_a_gloss: But for us a few things from many must be said toward the things set forth, refuting (διελέγχουσι) the ungrateful (ἀχάριστον) false opinion (ψευδοδοξία) toward the one who made (πεποιηκότα) him; for Celsus too, being 'a man', 'being in honour (ἐν τιμῇ) did not understand (οὐ συνῆκε)', wherefore he was not even 'compared (παρασυνεβλήθη)' with the birds and the other (irrational) animals which he thinks to be prophetic, but having yielded (παραχωρήσας) to them the first places (πρωτεῖα), beyond (ὑπέρ) the Egyptians who worship (προσκυνοῦντας) irrational animals as gods, he subjected (ὑπέταξε) himself, and as far as in him [lay] also the whole race of men, as worse (χεῖρον) and lesser (ἔλαττον) in thinking (νοοῦν) about the divine, to the irrational animals. First (προηγουμένως) then let it be inquired whether the divination through birds and the other animals believed (πεπιστευμένων) to be prophetic exists or does not exist. For not easily despised (εὐκαταφρόνητος) is the argument attempted (ἐπιχειρούμενος) to either side: on one side pressing/shaming (δυσωπῶν) [one] not to accept such a thing, lest the rational [being] (τὸ λογικόν) instead of the demonic oracles (δαιμόνια χρηστήρια) use birds, having left (καταλιπόν) those; on the other side, through vivid evidence (ἐνάργεια) witnessed by many, presenting that many were saved (διεσώθησαν) from greatest dangers, persuaded by the divination through birds. For the present let it be granted augury (οἰωνιστική) to be real (ὑπαρκτόν), so that even so I may show to those preoccupied/prejudiced (προκαταληφθεῖσιν) that even with this granted the superiority (ὑπεροχή) of man over irrational animals, even over the prophetic themselves, is great and in no way comparable (συγκριτή) to them. It must be said then that, if some divine nature (θεία φύσις) were in them foreknowing (προγνωστική) the future and so rich (πλουσία) as from abundance (περιουσία) to show also to whoever of men wishes the things to come, clearly much earlier they knew the things about themselves; and knowing the things about themselves they would have guarded against (ἐφυλάξατο) flying up over this place, on which men set snares (παγίδες) and nets (δίκτυα) against them, or archers, using as target (σκοπός) the flying, loosed arrows at them. And certainly eagles, foreknowing the plot (ἐπιβουλή) against the nestlings, whether of snakes climbing up to them and destroying them, or also of some men taking them either for play (παιδιά) or for some other use (χρεία) and service/care (θεραπεία), would not have nested where they were going to be plotted against; and in a word never would any of these animals be catchable (ἁλωτόν) by men, as more divine and wiser than men.
pass_b_english: We, for our part, must say a few things out of many in answer to what is before us, so as to refute his false opinion, ungrateful as it is toward the One who made him. For Celsus too, being “a man” who was “in honour,” “did not understand” (Psalm 49:20). That is why he was not even “compared” (Psalm 49:20) with the birds and the other irrational animals that he thinks prophetic. Instead, yielding them the first place, and going further than the Egyptians, who worship irrational animals as gods, he made himself subject to the irrational animals, and, as far as it lay with him, the whole human race too, as though it thought worse and less about the divine than they do.

First of all, then, let it be asked whether divination through birds and the other animals believed to be prophetic exists or does not exist. For the argument advanced on either side is not easy to despise. On the one hand, it urges us not to accept such a thing, so that the rational creature may not abandon the oracles of demons and use birds in their place. On the other hand, it presents the evidence, attested by many, that many people have been saved from the greatest dangers by trusting divination through birds.

For the present, let it be granted that augury is real, so that even so I may show those already prejudiced in its favour that, even if this is granted, man’s superiority over the irrational animals, even over the prophetic ones themselves, is great and beyond any comparison with them. We must say, then, that if there were in them some divine nature that foreknew the future, and so rich that out of its abundance it could show what is to come even to any man who wished, plainly they would have known their own affairs much sooner. And knowing their own affairs, they would have taken care not to fly up over a place where men had set snares and nets against them, or where archers, taking aim at flying creatures, were loosing arrows at them. Surely eagles too, if they foreknew the plot against their young, whether of snakes that climb up to them and destroy them or of men who take them for sport or for some other use and keeping, would not have nested where they were going to be plotted against. And, in a word, none of these animals would ever have been caught by men, if it were more divine and wiser than men.

choices.choice: 'the ungrateful false opinion he holds toward the One who made him' to 'his false opinion, ungrateful as it is toward the One who made him' (ἀχάριστον πρὸς τὸν πεποιηκότα: the ingratitude is toward the Maker)
Psalm clause: 'being “a man,” “in honour did not understand”' (calque) to 'being “a man” who was “in honour,” “did not understand”'; checked against LXX Psalm 48:13/21 = English Psalm 49:12/20
ὑπὲρ Αἰγυπτίους: 'beyond even the Egyptians' to 'going further than the Egyptians, who worship ...'
χεῖρον καὶ ἔλαττον νοοῦν taken together: 'as worse than they and as thinking less' to 'as though it thought worse and less about the divine than they do'
Removed added 'only' in 'forsake the oracles of demons only to use birds'; 'rational being' to 'rational creature'
προκαταληφθεῖσιν: 'those who have been taken in beforehand' to 'those already prejudiced in its favour'
οὐδαμῶς ... συγκριτή: 'in no way comparable with them' to 'beyond any comparison with them' (removes the ambiguity that the superiority is not comparable)

Scripture: “a man … in honour did not understand … was compared” comes from the Septuagint, Psalm 48:13 and 48:21 (ἄνθρωπος ἐν τιμῇ ὢν οὐ συνῆκεν, παρασυνεβλήθη τοῖς κτήνεσι τοῖς ἀνοήτοις), English Bible numbering Psalm 49:12 and 49:20. The LXX wording of the two verses is the same; the Hebrew of 49:20 (“does not understand”) matches the Greek more closely than 49:12 (“does not abide”), so Psalm 49:20 is cited, with 49:12 as the parallel. Koetschau marks ἄνθρωπος and ἐν τιμῇ ὢν οὐ συνῆκε as quoted; ἐν τιμῇ ὢν is rendered “who was ‘in honour’”. Origen turns the verse round: the Psalm says man was compared with the beasts, while Celsus did not even rank himself alongside them but put himself below them. ὑπὲρ Αἰγυπτίους: “going further than the Egyptians”. χεῖρον καὶ ἔλαττον νοοῦν taken together (thinking worse and less about the divine). τὸ δ᾿ ὅσον ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ: “as far as it lay with him”. (ἀλόγοις), (γινώσκον)τα and ἐφυλάξατο (ἂν): Koetschau’s supplements; translated as supplied. The printed ουν in “λεκτέον ουν” lacks its accent in the staged text; read as οὖν. ἵνα μὴ τὸ λογικὸν … καταλιπὸν ἐκεῖνα taken as: lest the rational creature, having left the demon oracles, use birds instead of them. προκαταληφθεῖσιν rendered “those already prejudiced in its favour” (in favour of augury, from the context). θεραπεία here probably “keeping/tending” (of captured eaglets); “service” possible. The chapter continues into 4.91, where Origen takes up Celsus’s claim about birds fighting birds, with Homer’s omens.
